verdict: OK to lend in Kozhikode wooden & modular furniture — favour organised modular/contract-fitout units with clean fire compliance and tight working-capital control; avoid pure sawmill-style carpentry shops with no fire cover or documented timber sourcing.
title: Kozhikode wooden & modular furniture: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A furniture unit here buys timber, plywood and hardware, converts them through carpentry, finishing and assembly, and sells either as retail home furniture or as modular fit-outs for homes, offices and hotels.** Cash comes in on delivery or on milestone billing for fit-outs; cash goes out upfront to timber auctions and plywood/hardware dealers. The Chaliyam depot in Kozhikode runs teak log auctions, and a record-breaking auction was reported in April 2026 [1] — so raw-material cost is set locally at auction, not by the borrower. **When a proposal lands, ask what share of timber is bought at auction versus from dealers, and get the last three purchase invoices.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in design, finishing and installation, not in the wood itself.** Peer Dhabriya Polywood says modular furniture is design- and execution-led and that the segment has many unorganised and big organised players [5]; the handicraft/furniture trade is fragmented with small-to-medium entities holding small shares [8]. **So pricing power is thin on commodity furniture and real only on design-led modular work — check the order book mix, not just turnover.** Working capital is the risk: timber and plywood are paid for early, retail and fit-out receivables come later. **Take stock statements and debtor ageing monthly; if auction purchases are funded on cash credit without matching sales, ask for the sales register against those lots.**

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is positive: Kerala GST collections grew 10.3% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide furniture-linked IIP (NIC 31) is up 9.4% YoY with 7.4% Apr-to-date [D].** Kerala electricity demand is up 11.1% Apr-to-date versus India's 9.5% [D] — neutral, but consistent with factories running. Against that, a fire destroyed a furniture factory at Chunkam, Feroke, with finished stock worth about one crore rupees reported [2] — a February 2025 report, so treat it as a standing local hazard, not fresh news. **Fire is the single biggest loss event in this trade; make fire compliance a condition, not a nicety.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue organised modular-fitout units with design capability, repeat institutional clients and documented timber sourcing; peer Dhabriya won a Rs 25.30 crore order from the Godrej Group [3], showing organised players can win large contracts.** Greenply's Q2FY27 topline rose 16.1% YoY with EBITDA margins at 11.2% [6] — a useful benchmark for what a well-run board/furniture player earns. **Avoid pure retail carpentry shops with no fire cover, no GST trail on timber and single-customer dependence.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure term loans for machinery/finishing equipment and cash credit for timber and plywood, with a drawing power tied to paid stock.** Take fire insurance assignment to the bank, GST returns monthly, stock and debtor statements monthly, and auction/dealer invoices quarterly. **If insurance lapses or stock cover falls below drawing power for two months, freeze the limit and inspect the unit.**

## Early warnings to watch
- **Monthly GST returns:** two consecutive months of falling turnover against stock build-up -> ask for sales register and inspect godown.
- **Monthly stock statement:** paid stock below drawing power -> reduce limit and seek fresh invoices.
- **Quarterly debtor ageing:** top customer above a third of receivables -> seek diversification plan or cap exposure.
- **Annual fire inspection:** lapsed policy or no hydrant/exit compliance -> make renewal conditional on rectification.
- **Quarterly auction invoices:** timber bought at auction but not reflected in production -> query diversion.
watch: Two months of falling turnover with rising stock -> inspect godown and ask for sales register
Paid stock below drawing power -> cut limit, demand fresh invoices
Single customer above one-third of receivables -> cap exposure, seek diversification
Lapsed policy or missing fire compliance -> make renewal conditional on rectification
Auction timber not matched to production -> query diversion of stock
